claim: Cerebral small vessel disease (SVD) is a leading cause of stroke and dementia.
source: Cerebral small vessel disease (SVD) is a leading cause of stroke and dementia.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about SVD.

claim: CADASIL is an inherited SVD that alters cerebral artery function, compromising blood flow to the working brain.
source: CADASIL, an inherited SVD, alters cerebral artery function, compromising blood flow to the working brain.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as background information about CADASIL.

claim: TIMP3 accumulation in the vascular extracellular matrix in CADASIL is a key contributor to cerebrovascular dysfunction.
source: TIMP3 (tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinase 3) accumulation in the vascular extracellular matrix in CADASIL is a key contributor to cerebrovascular dysfunction.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by prior work referenced in the introduction.

claim: TIMP3 acts through inhibition of the metalloprotease ADAM17 and HB-EGF to regulate cerebral arterial tone and blood flow responses.
source: TIMP3 acts through inhibition of the metalloprotease ADAM17 and HB-EGF to regulate cerebral arterial tone and blood flow responses.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Exogenous ADAM17 restores cerebral arterial tone and blood flow responses in a CADASIL mouse model.
source: In a clinically relevant CADASIL mouse model, we show that exogenous ADAM17 or HB-EGF restores cerebral arterial tone and blood flow responses
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figures 2 and 6.

claim: Exogenous HB-EGF restores cerebral arterial tone and blood flow responses in a CADASIL mouse model.
source: In a clinically relevant CADASIL mouse model, we show that exogenous ADAM17 or HB-EGF restores cerebral arterial tone and blood flow responses
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figures 4 and 6.

claim: Upregulated voltage-dependent potassium channel (KV) number in cerebral arterial myocytes is a downstream effector of TIMP3-induced deficits.
source: identify upregulated voltage-dependent potassium channel (KV) number in cerebral arterial myocytes as a heretofore-unrecognized downstream effector of TIMP3-induced deficits.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 7.

claim: The balance of TIMP3 and ADAM17 activity modulates CBF through regulation of myocyte KV channel number.
source: These results support the concept that the balance of TIMP3 and ADAM17 activity modulates CBF through regulation of myocyte KV channel number.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the abstract based on the experimental findings.

claim: Small vessel disease (SVD) of the brain is a leading cause of stroke and age-related cognitive decline and disability.
source: Small vessel disease (SVD) of the brain is a leading cause of stroke and age-related cognitive decline and disability for which there are currently no treatments (Pantoni, 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: There are currently no treatments for cerebral SVD.
source: Small vessel disease (SVD) of the brain is a leading cause of stroke and age-related cognitive decline and disability for which there are currently no treatments (Pantoni, 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: Limited understanding of the pathogenesis of cerebral SVD is a major obstacle to the development of treatments.
source: Our limited understanding of the pathogenesis of cerebral SVD is a major obstacle to the development of treatments.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a rationale for the study.

claim: CADASIL is the most common hereditary cerebral SVD.
source: CADASIL, the most common hereditary cerebral SVD, is caused by dominant mutations in the NOTCH3 receptor that stereotypically lead to the extracellular deposition of NOTCH3 ectodomain (Notch3ECD) and aggregates of other proteins on vessels (Joutel et al., 2000; Chabriat et al., 2009; Monet-Leprêtre et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: CADASIL is caused by dominant mutations in the NOTCH3 receptor.
source: CADASIL, the most common hereditary cerebral SVD, is caused by dominant mutations in the NOTCH3 receptor that stereotypically lead to the extracellular deposition of NOTCH3 ectodomain (Notch3ECD) and aggregates of other proteins on vessels (Joutel et al., 2000; Chabriat et al., 2009; Monet-Leprêtre et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: CADASIL mutations lead to the extracellular deposition of NOTCH3 ectodomain (Notch3ECD) and aggregates of other proteins on vessels.
source: CADASIL, the most common hereditary cerebral SVD, is caused by dominant mutations in the NOTCH3 receptor that stereotypically lead to the extracellular deposition of NOTCH3 ectodomain (Notch3ECD) and aggregates of other proteins on vessels (Joutel et al., 2000; Chabriat et al., 2009; Monet-Leprêtre et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: A deficit in cerebral blood flow (CBF) hemodynamics is an early feature of CADASIL.
source: A deficit in cerebral blood flow (CBF) hemodynamics is an early feature of the disease, suggesting that cerebrovascular dysfunction may have a key role in disease pathogenesis (Chabriat et al., 2000; Pfefferkorn et al., 2001; Liem et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Cerebrovascular dysfunction may have a key role in CADASIL disease pathogenesis.
source: A deficit in cerebral blood flow (CBF) hemodynamics is an early feature of the disease, suggesting that cerebrovascular dysfunction may have a key role in disease pathogenesis (Chabriat et al., 2000; Pfefferkorn et al., 2001; Liem et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an inference from cited studies.

claim: Cerebral arteries exist in a partially constricted state called 'myogenic tone'.
source: Cerebral arteries exist in a partially constricted state called 'myogenic tone', which reflects an intrinsic contractile response of arterial myocytes to increases in intravascular pressure.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about cerebral arteries.

claim: Myogenic tone reflects an intrinsic contractile response of arterial myocytes to increases in intravascular pressure.
source: Cerebral arteries exist in a partially constricted state called 'myogenic tone', which reflects an intrinsic contractile response of arterial myocytes to increases in intravascular pressure.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Functional hyperemia serves to satisfy enhanced glucose and oxygen demands of active neurons.
source: This phenomenon, known as functional hyperemia, serves to satisfy enhanced glucose and oxygen demands of active neurons (Iadecola and Nedergaard, 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: Impaired functional hyperemia is an early and prominent feature of the TgNotch3R169C CADASIL mouse model.
source: Impaired functional hyperemia and CBF autoregulation, attenuated CBF responses to topical application of vasodilators, and diminished myogenic responses of cerebral arteries and arterioles are early and prominent features of the well-established TgNotch3R169C CADASIL mouse model (Joutel et al., 2010; Dabertrand et al., 2015; Capone et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: Impaired CBF autoregulation is an early and prominent feature of the TgNotch3R169C CADASIL mouse model.
source: Impaired functional hyperemia and CBF autoregulation, attenuated CBF responses to topical application of vasodilators, and diminished myogenic responses of cerebral arteries and arterioles are early and prominent features of the well-established TgNotch3R169C CADASIL mouse model (Joutel et al., 2010; Dabertrand et al., 2015; Capone et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: Attenuated CBF responses to topical application of vasodilators is an early and prominent feature of the TgNotch3R169C CADASIL mouse model.
source: Impaired functional hyperemia and CBF autoregulation, attenuated CBF responses to topical application of vasodilators, and diminished myogenic responses of cerebral arteries and arterioles are early and prominent features of the well-established TgNotch3R169C CADASIL mouse model (Joutel et al., 2010; Dabertrand et al., 2015; Capone et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: Diminished myogenic responses of cerebral arteries and arterioles are early and prominent features of the TgNotch3R169C CADASIL mouse model.
source: Impaired functional hyperemia and CBF autoregulation, attenuated CBF responses to topical application of vasodilators, and diminished myogenic responses of cerebral arteries and arterioles are early and prominent features of the well-established TgNotch3R169C CADASIL mouse model (Joutel et al., 2010; Dabertrand et al., 2015; Capone et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: TIMP3 forms complexes with Notch3ECD and abnormally accumulates in the extracellular matrix of brain vessels of patients and mice with CADASIL.
source: Recently, we found that TIMP3 (tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinases-3) forms complexes with Notch3ECD and abnormally accumulates in the extracellular matrix of brain vessels of patients and mice with CADASIL (Monet-Leprêtre et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claim: Genetic overexpression of TIMP3 recapitulates both CBF and myogenic-response deficits of the CADASIL model.
source: Remarkably, genetic overexpression of TIMP3 recapitulates both CBF and myogenic-response deficits of the CADASIL model; conversely, genetic reduction of TIMP3 in CADASIL model mice restores normal function (Capone et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claim: Genetic reduction of TIMP3 in CADASIL model mice restores normal function.
source: Remarkably, genetic overexpression of TIMP3 recapitulates both CBF and myogenic-response deficits of the CADASIL model; conversely, genetic reduction of TIMP3 in CADASIL model mice restores normal function (Capone et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claim: TIMP3 has the broadest spectrum of substrates within the TIMP family.
source: Within the TIMP family, TIMP3 has the broadest spectrum of substrates, which extends to members of the ADAM (a disintegrin and metalloproteinases) family.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about TIMP3.

claim: ADAM metalloproteinases proteolytically release the extracellular domains of membrane-bound cytokines, cell adhesion molecules and growth factors.
source: These metalloproteinases proteolytically release the extracellular domains of membrane-bound cytokines, cell adhesion molecules and growth factors, such as tumor necrosis factor-α and several ligands of the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) family, including HB-EGF (heparin-binding EGF-like growth factor) (Brew and Nagase, 2010; Khokha et al., 2013; Arpino et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Upregulation of voltage-gated potassium (KV) channels at the plasma membrane of arterial myocytes is responsible for the diminished myogenic responses of cerebral arteries and penetrating arterioles in the TgNotch3R169C CADASIL model.
source: In another recent study, we established that upregulation of voltage-gated potassium (KV) channels at the plasma membrane of arterial myocytes is responsible for the diminished myogenic responses of cerebral arteries and penetrating arterioles in the TgNotch3R169C CADASIL model.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a reference to prior work.

claim: An influence of the endothelium in myogenic tone deficit was ruled out in the TgNotch3R169C CADASIL model.
source: Notably, an influence of the endothelium in myogenic tone deficit was ruled out (Dabertrand et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claim: KV channels play an important and dynamic role in opposing pressure-induced depolarization and vasoconstriction.
source: KV channels play an important and dynamic role in opposing pressure-induced depolarization and vasoconstriction (Longden et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: Down-regulation of plasma membrane KV channels through activation of the EGFR pathway restores normal responses to pressure in the CADASIL model.
source: Furthermore, we (Dabertrand et al., 2015) and our collaborators (Koide et al., 2007) have found that down-regulation of plasma membrane KV channels through activation of the EGFR pathway restores normal responses to pressure.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: TIMP3 (40 nM) did not affect resting CBF in wild-type mice.
source: We found that TIMP3 (40 nM) did not affect resting CBF (Figure 1B)
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: TIMP3 (40 nM) strongly reduced the increase in CBF evoked by whisker stimulation in wild-type mice.
source: We found that TIMP3 (40 nM) did not affect resting CBF (Figure 1B), but did strongly reduce the increase in CBF evoked by whisker stimulation (Figure 1C,D; Figure 1—source data 2,3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 1C and 1D.

claim: TIMP3 (8 nM) attenuated functional hyperemia in wild-type mice.
source: Superfusion of 8 nM TIMP3 similarly attenuated functional hyperemia (Figure 1—figure supplement 2; Figure 1—source data 2,3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The amplitude of the somatosensory field potentials produced by electrical stimulation of the whisker pad was unaltered by TIMP3 superfusion.
source: We found that the amplitude of the somatosensory fields potentials produced by electrical stimulation of the whisker pad was unaltered by TIMP3 superfusion (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Neither exogenous TIMP1 (50 nM) nor TIMP2 (50 nM) altered functional hyperemia in wild-type mice.
source: In sharp contrast to TIMP3, neither exogenous TIMP1 (50 nM) nor TIMP2 (50 nM) altered functional hyperemia (Figure 1C,D; Figure 1—source data 2,3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 1C and 1D.

claim: TIMP3 (8 and 40 nM) profoundly attenuated the increases in CBF induced by acetylcholine or adenosine.
source: Again, the increases in CBF induced by acetylcholine or adenosine were profoundly attenuated by TIMP3 but were unaffected by TIMP2 or TIMP1, with the exception of a modest attenuation of the adenosine-induced increase in CBF by TIMP1 (Figure 1G,H; Figure 1—figure supplement 2; Figure 1—source data 2,3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 1G, 1H, and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: TIMP2 and TIMP1 did not affect CBF responses to acetylcholine or adenosine, with the exception of a modest attenuation of the adenosine-induced increase in CBF by TIMP1.
source: Again, the increases in CBF induced by acetylcholine or adenosine were profoundly attenuated by TIMP3 but were unaffected by TIMP2 or TIMP1, with the exception of a modest attenuation of the adenosine-induced increase in CBF by TIMP1 (Figure 1G,H; Figure 1—figure supplement 2; Figure 1—source data 2,3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 1G, 1H, and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Elevation of TIMP3 is sufficient to induce CBF deficits in vivo.
source: Thus, these findings establish that elevation of TIMP3 is sufficient to induce CBF deficits in vivo and suggest that a TIMP3-specific target accounts for these deficits.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the experimental findings.

claim: A TIMP3-specific target accounts for CBF deficits induced by TIMP3.
source: Thus, these findings establish that elevation of TIMP3 is sufficient to induce CBF deficits in vivo and suggest that a TIMP3-specific target accounts for these deficits.
evidence: This is an inference stated in the results based on the differential effects of TIMP3 vs TIMP1/TIMP2.

claim: ADAM17 is expressed in brain arteries.
source: Our efforts to identify the target of TIMP3 focused on ADAM17, which is uniquely inhibited by TIMP3 (Xu et al., 2012) and is expressed in brain arteries, as demonstrated by our immunoblot analyses (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2A,B.

claim: ADAM17 is uniquely inhibited by TIMP3.
source: Our efforts to identify the target of TIMP3 focused on ADAM17, which is uniquely inhibited by TIMP3 (Xu et al., 2012) and is expressed in brain arteries, as demonstrated by our immunoblot analyses (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a citation.

claim: GW413333X (5 µM) strongly attenuated the increase in CBF produced by whisker stimulation or topical application of acetylcholine or adenosine.
source: We found that GW413333X (5 µM), but not GI254023X (5 and 20 µM), strongly attenuated the increase in CBF produced by whisker stimulation or topical application of acetylcholine or adenosine (Figure 2C–E; Figure 2—figure supplement 1A; Figure 2—source data 2,3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 2C-E and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: GI254023X (5 and 20 µM) did not attenuate the increase in CBF produced by whisker stimulation or topical application of acetylcholine or adenosine.
source: We found that GW413333X (5 µM), but not GI254023X (5 and 20 µM), strongly attenuated the increase in CBF produced by whisker stimulation or topical application of acetylcholine or adenosine (Figure 2C–E; Figure 2—figure supplement 1A; Figure 2—source data 2,3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 2C-E and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Genetic depletion of ADAM17 strongly attenuated CBF responses in a dose-dependent manner.
source: We found that genetic depletion of ADAM17 strongly attenuated CBF responses in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 2F,G; Figure 2—figure supplement 1B; Figure 2—source data 2,3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 2F,G and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Topical neocortical application of sADAM17 (16 nM) did not affect cerebrovascular responses in wild-type mice.
source: Topical neocortical application of sADAM17 (16 nM) (Figure 2—source data 1) did not affect cerebrovascular responses in wild-type mice, but did fully restore CBF responses in Adam17ex/+ mice with half-reduced ADAM17 levels (Figure 2H–J; Figure 2—figures supplements 1C,2A; Figure 2—source data 2,3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 2H-J.

claim: Topical neocortical application of sADAM17 (16 nM) fully restored CBF responses in Adam17ex/+ mice with half-reduced ADAM17 levels.
source: Topical neocortical application of sADAM17 (16 nM) (Figure 2—source data 1) did not affect cerebrovascular responses in wild-type mice, but did fully restore CBF responses in Adam17ex/+ mice with half-reduced ADAM17 levels (Figure 2H–J; Figure 2—figures supplements 1C,2A; Figure 2—source data 2,3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 2H-J.

claim: Decreasing ADAM17 activity compromises CBF regulation.
source: Together, these results indicate that decreasing ADAM17 activity compromises CBF regulation.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the experimental findings.

claim: Neocortical application of the selective ErbB1/EGFR and ErbB4 inhibitor, tyrphostin AG1478 (10 and 20 µM), strongly attenuated the evoked CBF responses.
source: Indeed, we found that neocortical application of the selective ErbB1/EGFR and ErbB4 inhibitor, tyrphostin AG1478 (10 and 20 µM), strongly attenuated the evoked CBF responses, but did not impair resting CBF.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3C-E.

claim: Tyrphostin AG1478 (10 and 20 µM) did not impair resting CBF.
source: Indeed, we found that neocortical application of the selective ErbB1/EGFR and ErbB4 inhibitor, tyrphostin AG1478 (10 and 20 µM), strongly attenuated the evoked CBF responses, but did not impair resting CBF.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3C.

claim: CBF responses were unaffected by the selective ErbB2 inhibitor, tyrphostin AG825, at both 50 and 200 µM.
source: In contrast, CBF responses were unaffected by the selective ErbB2 inhibitor, tyrphostin AG825, at both 50 and 200 µM (Figure 3C–E; Figure 3—source data 2, 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3C-E.

claim: Evoked CBF responses were attenuated by superfusion of either ErbB1/EGFR (67 nM) or ErbB4 (71 nM) receptor traps.
source: Evoked CBF responses were attenuated by superfusion of either ErbB1/EGFR (67 nM) or ErbB4 (71 nM) receptor traps, which block the function of ErbB1 and ErbB4 ligands, respectively, but not by superfusion of the ErbB3 (71 nM) receptor trap or by control IgG1 Fc (286 nM) and IgG2 Fc (286 nM) fragments (Figure 3F–H; Figure 3—figure supplement 1A; Figure 3—source data 2, 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 3F-H.

claim: Evoked CBF responses were not attenuated by superfusion of the ErbB3 (71 nM) receptor trap or by control IgG1 Fc (286 nM) and IgG2 Fc (286 nM) fragments.
source: Evoked CBF responses were attenuated by superfusion of either ErbB1/EGFR (67 nM) or ErbB4 (71 nM) receptor traps, which block the function of ErbB1 and ErbB4 ligands, respectively, but not by superfusion of the ErbB3 (71 nM) receptor trap or by control IgG1 Fc (286 nM) and IgG2 Fc (286 nM) fragments (Figure 3F–H; Figure 3—figure supplement 1A; Figure 3—source data 2, 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 3F-H.

claim: The effects of ErbB1 and ErbB4 receptor traps on evoked CBF responses were not additive.
source: Notably, the effects of ErbB1 and ErbB4 receptor traps on evoked CBF responses were not additive (Figure 3G–H; Figure 3—source data 2, 3), even though neither ErbB1 nor ErbB4 receptor traps achieved maximum inhibition.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 3G-H.

claim: Superfusion of heparin (40 ui/mL) impaired evoked CBF responses without affecting resting CBF.
source: We found that superfusion of heparin (40 ui/mL), which competitively inhibits binding of HB-EGF to cell surface HSPGs (Higashiyama et al., 1993), impaired evoked CBF responses without affecting resting CBF (Figure 3I–K; Figure 3—figure supplement 1B; Figure 3—source data 2, 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 3I-K.

claim: Superfusion of p21 (12 µM) impaired evoked CBF responses without affecting resting CBF.
source: We found that superfusion of p21 (12 µM) similarly impaired evoked CBF responses without affecting resting CBF (Figure 3I–K; Figure 3—figure supplement 1B; Figure 3—source data 2, 3); in contrast, a mutated inactive p21 peptide (p21-mut; 12 µM) had no effect on evoked or resting CBF.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 3I-K.

claim: A mutated inactive p21 peptide (p21-mut; 12 µM) had no effect on evoked or resting CBF.
source: We found that superfusion of p21 (12 µM) similarly impaired evoked CBF responses without affecting resting CBF (Figure 3I–K; Figure 3—figure supplement 1B; Figure 3—source data 2, 3); in contrast, a mutated inactive p21 peptide (p21-mut; 12 µM) had no effect on evoked or resting CBF.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 3I-K.

claim: sHB-EGF (20 nM) prevented TIMP3-induced cerebrovascular deficits.
source: We found that sHB-EGF (20 nM) prevented TIMP3 and GW-induced cerebrovascular deficits (Figure 4D–I; Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B; Figure 4—source data 2,3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 4D-I.

claim: sHB-EGF (20 nM) prevented GW413333X-induced cerebrovascular deficits.
source: We found that sHB-EGF (20 nM) prevented TIMP3 and GW-induced cerebrovascular deficits (Figure 4D–I; Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B; Figure 4—source data 2,3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 4G-I.

claim: sHB-EGF significantly improved evoked CBF responses in Adam17ex/ex mice.
source: Also, sHB-EGF significantly improved evoked CBF responses in Adam17ex/ex mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: sHB-EGF could not prevent CBF deficits induced by pharmacological blockage of ErbB1/EGFR and ErbB4.
source: Notably, sHB-EGF could not prevent CBF deficits induced by pharmacological blockage of ErbB1/EGFR and ErbB4 (Figure 4A–C; Figure 4—source data 1–3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 4A-C.

claim: ADAM17/HB-EGF/(ErbB1/ErbB4) is a key TIMP3-sensitive signaling pathway for cerebrovascular regulation.
source: These findings, collectively, suggest that ADAM17/HB-EGF/(ErbB1/ErbB4) is a key TIMP3-sensitive signaling pathway for cerebrovascular regulation.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the experimental findings.

claim: Pre-incubation of arterial segments with TIMP3 (8 nM) strongly attenuated myogenic tone at pressures of 40 mmHg and above compared to arteries incubated with vehicle.
source: We found that pre-incubation of arterial segments with TIMP3 (8 nM) strongly attenuated myogenic tone at pressures of 40 mmHg and above compared to arteries incubated with vehicle, whereas recombinant TIMP2 (10 nM) had no effect (Figure 5A–C; Figure 5—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 5A-C.

claim: Recombinant TIMP2 (10 nM) had no effect on myogenic tone.
source: We found that pre-incubation of arterial segments with TIMP3 (8 nM) strongly attenuated myogenic tone at pressures of 40 mmHg and above compared to arteries incubated with vehicle, whereas recombinant TIMP2 (10 nM) had no effect (Figure 5A–C; Figure 5—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 5A-C.

claim: Attenuation of myogenic responses by TIMP3 was even more pronounced in intracerebral penetrating arterioles.
source: Notably, attenuation of myogenic responses by TIMP3 was even more pronounced in intracerebral penetrating arterioles (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Myogenic constriction to pressure was strongly attenuated by the dual ADAM10/ADAM17 inhibitor GW413333X (1 µM).
source: Likewise, myogenic constriction to pressure was strongly attenuated by the dual ADAM10/ADAM17 inhibitor GW413333X (1 µM), but not by the ADAM10 inhibitor GI254023X (1 µM).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Myogenic constriction to pressure was not attenuated by the ADAM10 inhibitor GI254023X (1 µM).
source: Likewise, myogenic constriction to pressure was strongly attenuated by the dual ADAM10/ADAM17 inhibitor GW413333X (1 µM), but not by the ADAM10 inhibitor GI254023X (1 µM).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Myogenic tone was reduced in heterozygous ADAM17 hypomorphic mice (Adam17ex/+) compared to wild-type littermates (Adam17+/+).
source: Also, myogenic tone was reduced in heterozygous ADAM17 hypomorphic mice (Adam17ex/+) compared to wild-type littermates (Adam17+/+) but restored by pre-incubating arterial segments of Adam17ex/+ mice with sADAM17 (3.2 nM) (Figure 5D,I; Figure 5—figure supplement 2; Figure 5—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 5D,I.

claim: Myogenic tone in Adam17ex/+ mice was restored by pre-incubating arterial segments with sADAM17 (3.2 nM).
source: Also, myogenic tone was reduced in heterozygous ADAM17 hypomorphic mice (Adam17ex/+) compared to wild-type littermates (Adam17+/+) but restored by pre-incubating arterial segments of Adam17ex/+ mice with sADAM17 (3.2 nM) (Figure 5D,I; Figure 5—figure supplement 2; Figure 5—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 5I and Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Pre-incubation of arteries with the ErbB1/ErbB4 inhibitor AG1478 (2 µM) strongly attenuated myogenic responses.
source: Moreover, pre-incubation of arteries with the ErbB1/ErbB4 inhibitor AG1478 (2 µM) or the HB-EGF inhibitor p21 peptide (2.4 µM), but not with the p21-mut peptide (2.4 µM), strongly attenuated myogenic responses (Figure 5E,F; Figure 5—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 5E,F.

claim: Pre-incubation of arteries with the HB-EGF inhibitor p21 peptide (2.4 µM) strongly attenuated myogenic responses.
source: Moreover, pre-incubation of arteries with the ErbB1/ErbB4 inhibitor AG1478 (2 µM) or the HB-EGF inhibitor p21 peptide (2.4 µM), but not with the p21-mut peptide (2.4 µM), strongly attenuated myogenic responses (Figure 5E,F; Figure 5—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 5E,F.

claim: Pre-incubation of arteries with the p21-mut peptide (2.4 µM) did not attenuate myogenic responses.
source: Moreover, pre-incubation of arteries with the ErbB1/ErbB4 inhibitor AG1478 (2 µM) or the HB-EGF inhibitor p21 peptide (2.4 µM), but not with the p21-mut peptide (2.4 µM), strongly attenuated myogenic responses (Figure 5E,F; Figure 5—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 5E,F.

claim: Myogenic tone is increased by tonic activity of the ADAM17/HB-EGF/(ErbB1/ErbB4) pathway.
source: Thus, these data indicate that myogenic tone is increased by tonic activity of the ADAM17/HB-EGF/(ErbB1/ErbB4) pathway.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the experimental findings.

claim: Co-incubation of arterial segments with sHB-EGF (3 nM) significantly ameliorated the TIMP3-induced reduction in arterial tone.
source: We found that co-incubation of arterial segments with sHB-EGF significantly ameliorated the TIMP3-induced reduction in arterial tone (Figure 5G; Figure 5—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5G.

claim: Co-incubation of arterial segments with sHB-EGF (3 nM) overcame the reduction in arterial tone caused by GW413333-mediated inhibition of ADAM17.
source: Likewise, co-incubation of arterial segments with sHB-EGF overcame the reduction in arterial tone caused by GW413333-mediated inhibition of ADAM17 (Figure 5H; Figure 5—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5H.

claim: sHB-EGF (3 nM) significantly increased myogenic tone in arteries from heterozygous ADAM17-hypomorphic mice (Adam17ex/+), restoring a near-normal myogenic phenotype.
source: Moreover, sHB-EGF significantly increased myogenic tone in arteries from heterozygous ADAM17-hypomorphic mice (Adam17ex/+), restoring a near-normal myogenic phenotype (Figure 5I; Figure 5—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5I.

claim: The TIMP3-sensitive pathway, ADAM17/HB-EGF/(ErbB1/ErbB4), increases myogenic constriction in brain arteries.

source: We found that preincubation of arterial segments with the enzymatically active extracellular domain of ADAM17 (3.2 nM) increased myogenic tone in arteries from TgNotch3R169C CADASIL mice, whereas sADAM17 had no detectable effect on arterial segments from wild-type mice at this concentration (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6A.

claim: sADAM17 (3.2 nM) had no detectable effect on arterial segments from wild-type mice.
source: We found that preincubation of arterial segments with the enzymatically active extracellular domain of ADAM17 (3.2 nM) increased myogenic tone in arteries from TgNotch3R169C CADASIL mice, whereas sADAM17 had no detectable effect on arterial segments from wild-type mice at this concentration (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6A.

claim: sADAM17 (16 nM), locally applied on the neocortex of TgNotch3R169C CADASIL mice, significantly improved resting CBF.
source: We further found that sADAM17 (16 nM), locally applied on the necortex of TgNotch3R169C CADASIL mice, significantly improved resting CBF and rescued the impaired reactivity of brain vessels to whisker stimulation and vasodilators (Figure 6B–D; Figure 6—figure supplement 1; Figure 6—source data 1,2).

claim: sADAM17 (16 nM), locally applied on the neocortex of TgNotch3R169C CADASIL mice, rescued the impaired reactivity of brain vessels to whisker stimulation and vasodilators.
source: We further found that sADAM17 (16 nM), locally applied on the necortex of TgNotch3R169C CADASIL mice, significantly improved resting CBF and rescued the impaired reactivity of brain vessels to whisker stimulation and vasodilators (Figure 6B–D; Figure 6—figure supplement 1; Figure 6—source data 1,2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 6B-D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Exogenous sHB-EGF (20 nM) restored evoked CBF responses in TgNotch3R169C mice.
source: Here, we extend these observations, showing that exogenous sHB-EGF (20 nM) restored evoked CBF responses in TgNotch3R169C mice (Figure 6E–G; Figure 6—source data 1,2).

claim: The diminished myogenic tone and CBF deficits in CADASIL are caused by TIMP3-mediated suppression of the ADAM17/HB-EGF/(ErbB1/ErbB4) pathway.
source: Collectively, these findings support the concept that the diminished myogenic tone and CBF deficits in CADASIL are caused by TIMP3-mediated suppression of the ADAM17/HB-EGF/(ErbB1/ErbB4) pathway.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the experimental findings.

claim: KV current density was significantly lower in myocytes from TgNotch3R169C;Timp3+/- mice than in myocytes from TgNotch3R169C;Timp3+/+ at all voltage steps above +10 mV.
source: We found that KV current density was significantly lower in myocytes from TgNotch3R169C;Timp3+/- mice than in myocytes from TgNotch3R169C;Timp3+/+ at all voltage steps above +10 mV (Figure 7A–C; Figure 7—source data 2).

claim: Incubation of wild-type arterial myocytes with recombinant TIMP3 (8 nM) resulted in a significant increase in KV current density compared with myocytes incubated with vehicle.
source: Conversely, incubation of wild-type arterial myocytes with recombinant TIMP3 (8 nM) resulted in a significant increase in KV current density compared with myocytes incubated with vehicle (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A,B; Figure 7—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: The TIMP3 pathway regulates the number of KV channels, and not channel properties.
source: These results indicate that the TIMP3 pathway regulates the number of channels, and not channel properties (Figure 7—figure supplement 2; Figure 7—source data 1,2).
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the analysis of channel kinetics shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: Exogenously applied TIMP3 increased the number of KV channels in arteries from wild-type mice by ~25% (from 3120 to 3920 per myocyte).
source: This analysis showed that exogenously applied TIMP3 increased the number of KV channels in arteries from wild-type mice by ~25% (from 3120 to 3920 per myocyte).
evidence: This is stated in the results based on calculations using the Goldman–Hodgkin–Katz constant field equation.

claim: In the TIMP3-overexpressing TgNotch3R169C;Timp3+/+ genetic model, KV channel density (4840/myocyte) was ~38% greater than that in TgNotch3R169C;Timp3+/- mice (3510/myocyte).
source: A similar increase in KV channel number was observed in the TIMP3-overexpressing TgNotch3R169C;Timp3+/+ genetic model, where channel density (4840/myocyte) was ~38% greater than that in TgNotch3R169C;Timp3+/- mice (3510/myocyte).
evidence: This is stated in the results based on calculations using the Goldman–Hodgkin–Katz constant field equation.

claim: Application of enzymatically active, sADAM17 (3.2 nM) significantly reduced KV current density in TgNotch3R169C cerebral myocytes, decreasing the density of Kv channels by ~22% (from 4840 to 3760 channels per myocyte).
source: Consistent with the ability of exogenous sADAM17 to restore normal myogenic responses in TgNotch3R169C mice, we found that application of enzymatically active, sADAM17 (3.2 nM) significantly reduced KV current density in TgNotch3R169C cerebral myocytes, decreasing the density of Kv channels by ~22% (from 4840 to 3760 channels per myocyte) (Figure 7D,E; Figure 7—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 7D,E.

claim: Excess TIMP3 in the TgNotch3R169C CADASIL model drives increased KV channel density and diminished myogenic responses by reducing ADAM17 activity and subsequently reducing the release of sHB-EGF.
source: Thus, these new findings, taken together with our previous studies, indicate that excess TIMP3 in the TgNotch3R169CCADASILmodel drives increased KV channel density and diminished myogenic responses by reducing ADAM17 activity and subsequently reducing the release of sHB-EGF.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the experimental findings.

claim: A TIMP3-sensitive pathway is constitutively engaged in the regulation of cerebral hemodynamics.
source: In the present study, we establish the novel concept that a TIMP3-sensitive pathway is constitutively engaged in the regulation of cerebral hemodynamics, and we unravel the mechanism by which excess TIMP3 in brain vessels compromises cerebrovascular regulation in a clinically relevant model of CADASIL.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the discussion.

claim: ADAM17/HB-EGF/(ErbB1/ErbB4) is a key TIMP3-sensitive signaling module essential for maintaining robust CBF responses to evoked neural activity or topically applied vasodilators as well as for myogenic responses of brain arteries.
source: By combining genetic and pharmacological approaches with in vivo analyses of CBF regulation and ex vivo measurements of myogenic responses of brain arteries in physiological settings, we found that ADAM17/HB-EGF/(ErbB1/ErbB4) is a key TIMP3-sensitive signaling module essential for maintaining robust CBF responses to evoked neural activity or topically applied vasodilators as well as for myogenic responses of brain arteries.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the discussion.

claim: In the setting of CADASIL, attenuated ADAM17 and HB-EGF-dependent activation of ErbB1/ErbB4 underlies deficits in evoked CBF responses and cerebral arterial tone.
source: Next, using the TgNotch3R169C model, we provided pharmacological evidence that, in the setting of CADASIL, attenuated ADAM17 and HB-EGF-dependent activation of ErbB1/ErbB4 underlies deficits in evoked CBF responses and cerebral arterial tone.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the discussion.

claim: Elevated TIMP3 blunts the activity of the ADAM17/HB-EGF/(ErbB1/ErbB4) pathway in cerebral arterial myocytes, thereby attenuating myogenic responses in brain arteries and compromising CBF regulation in CADASIL.
source: Collectively, these data suggest that elevated TIMP3 blunts the activity of the ADAM17/HB-EGF/(ErbB1/ErbB4) pathway in cerebral arterial myocytes, thereby attenuating myogenic responses in brain arteries and compromising CBF regulation in CADASIL (Figure 8).
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the discussion and illustrated in Figure 8.

claim: Under physiological conditions, tonic activity of the ADAM17/HB-EGF/(ErbB1/ErbB4) pathway prevents excess accumulation of KV channels at the plasma membrane and thereby maintains myogenic tone and robust CBF responses to neural activity and vasodilators.
source: Our results indicate that, under physiological conditions, tonic activity of the ADAM17/HB-EGF/(ErbB1/ErbB4) pathway prevents excess accumulation of KV channels at the plasma membrane and thereby maintains myogenic tone and robust CBF responses to neural activity and vasodilators.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the discussion based on the experimental findings.

claim: The set point of the ADAM17/HB-EGF/(ErbB1/ErbB4) pathway in a physiological in vivo setting is already at maximum.
source: This suggests that the set point of this pathway in a physiological in vivo setting is already at maximum.
evidence: This is an inference stated in the discussion based on the observation that activating the pathway did not enhance responses.

claim: KV current density in cerebral artery myocytes is at least 50% lower than that in peripheral artery myocytes.
source: On the other hand, decreasing KV current density in cerebral artery myocytes, which is at least 50% lower than that in peripheral artery myocytes (Dabertrand et al., 2015), could be an in vivo rate-limiting step following physiological activation of this pathway.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation to prior work.

claim: The blood component, oxyhemoglobin, causes suppression of KV currents in cerebral arterial myocytes through HB-EGF–mediated activation of ErbB1/ErbB4, resulting in membrane depolarization and enhanced tone of brain arteries.
source: Indeed, Wellman and colleagues have shown that the blood component, oxyhemoglobin, causes suppression of KV currents in cerebral arterial myocytes through HB-EGF–mediated activation of ErbB1/ErbB4, resulting in membrane depolarization and enhanced tone of brain arteries (Nystoriak et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation.

claim: Upregulation of KV channels is sufficient to explain the decrease in myogenic tone in the CADASIL model, without an involvement of the endothelium or large conductance, voltage and Ca2+ activated K+ (BK) channels.
source: Moreover, our previous (Dabertrand et al., 2015) and current results collectively indicate that upregulation of KV channels is sufficient to explain the decrease in myogenic tone, without an involvement of the endothelium or large conductance, voltage and Ca2+ activated K+ (BK) channels.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on prior and current findings.

claim: The reduction in myogenic tone caused by inhibition of the ADAM17/HB-EGF/(ErbB1/ErbB4) pathway by excess TIMP3 in the extracellular matrix surrounding smooth muscle cells likely accounts for the attenuation of evoked CBF responses in CADASIL.
source: Given the key role of KV channels in the regulation of arterial tone, these findings are consistent with the interpretation that the smooth muscle ADAM17/HB-EGF/(ErbB1/ErbB4)/KV pathway regulates evoked CBF responses by elevating the physiological tone of brain arteries, and that the reduction in myogenic tone caused by inhibition of this pathway by excess TIMP3 in the extracellular matrix surrounding smooth muscle cells likely accounts for the attenuation of evoked CBF responses in CADASIL (Figure 8).
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the discussion based on the experimental findings and illustrated in Figure 8.

claim: The initial degree of arteriolar tone determines the diameter changes elicited by functional hyperemia.
source: A previous study in acute brain slices provides additional support for this interpretation, showing that the initial degree of arteriolar tone determines the diameter changes elicited by functional hyperemia (Blanco et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation.

claim: ADAM17 activity depends on the relative activity of ADAM17 and TIMP3 in brain arteries.
source: The fact that increasing TIMP3 or decreasing ADAM17 caused a concentration-dependent impairment of cerebrovascular function taken together with the observation that exogenous sADAM17 is capable of overcoming elevated TIMP3-induced cerebrovascular dysfunction indicates that ADAM17 activity depends on the relative activity of ADAM17 and TIMP3 in brain arteries.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the discussion based on the experimental findings.

claim: The ratio of TIMP3 and ADAM17 at the cell surface is likely a key determinant of ADAM17 activity.
source: Thus, the ratio of TIMP3 and ADAM17 at the cell surface is likely a key determinant of ADAM17 activity.
evidence: This is an inference stated in the discussion based on evidence from cell systems.

source: In summary, our study has uncovered a novel and central role for the ADAM17/HB-EGF/ErbB/KV signaling pathway in the physiological and pathological control of CBF and arterial tone.

source: Our results highlight a heretofore-unrecognized mechanistic link between pathological alterations of the vascular extracellular matrix and KV channel density that underlies cerebrovascular dysfunction in CADASIL.
